To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cetrorelix treatment of the mare for 5 days beginning on Days 1-5 of the luteinizing hormone surge does not suppress gonadotropins to undetectable concentrations and 2) the FSH surge that precedes the next ovulation occurs only after a threshold of GnRH-induced FSH secretion is exceeded.

cetrorelix treatment during the early luteal phase had no effect on the inter-ovulatory period or the FSH concentrations preceding the next ovulation, whereas treatment at the mid- or entire luteal phases delayed ovulation and increased the FSH concentrations before the next ovulation.
the gonadotropins are suppressed by cetrorelix but not eliminated, and that FSH concentrations are higher at approximately 6- 10 days prior to the onset of estrus and ovulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of FSH and the role of FSH in ovarian function.
the role of GnRH in the control of FSH and ovulation, and the role of FSH in the control of ovulation.
the role of FSH in ovarian function in the mare and the present results show that FSH is required for ovulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the administration of the GnRH antagonist ceterorelix to mares in the mid-luteal phase of their cycle, when administered for 4-5 days or for the entire 16 days, will inhibit ovulation.

the administration of the GnRH antagonist to mares during the luteolysing phase of the estrus cycle does not affect the inter-ovulatory period, but does cause an increase in FSH concentrations at the time of the subsequent ovulation.
GnRH antagonists are effective inhibitors of the secretion of FSI and LH, but that the degree of inhibition and the time-course of this inhibition are not predictable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the administration of GnRH antagonists to mares at any time in the luteal or follicular phase can suppress the release of FSH and, to a lesser degree, LH.

the administration of a GnRH antagonist during the early luteal phase did not alter the inter-ovulatory period, and that the administration of cetroreliix in the mid-luteal phase did alter the inter- ovulatory period, but the administration of ceterorelix for the entire luteral phase altered the inter-ovlulatory period.

cetrorelix treatment during the luteolysin period (Days 1 to 16) did not affect the onset of luteolysis, but delayed its completion, which in turn, caused the luteal lifespan to be longer than controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timing of GnRH antagonist treatment during the luteol phase can affect the timing of the next ovulation in the mare.
cetrorelix is an effective antagonist of FSH and/or LH secretion in the mare.
the GnRH system is not a'switch' but rather is a complex system that is involved in many aspects of reproductive physiology and function.
